items.title: [Comment] Establishing cardiovascular safety of the small-molecule GLP-1 receptor agonist orforglipron in type 2 diabetes
items.summary: Cardiovascular outcomes trials with GLP-1 receptor agonists, which to date have largely comprised peptide analogues of the incretin hormone GLP-1, have evolved from studies primarily designed to establish cardiovascular safety to trials demonstrating cardiovascular benefit.1–3 Substantial reductions in major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) and kidney protection have been demonstrated with multiple GLP-1 receptor agonists for subcutaneous administration,1–3 and, more recently, with oral semaglutide.

items.title: [Comment] Making every vial count: fractional dosing of yellow fever vaccine

items.title: [Comment] Offline: In praise of astrologers, sorcerers, and magicians
items.summary: “Prophecies are the grounds on which fights over the future take place”, writes Carissa Véliz in Prophecy: Prediction, Power, and the Fight for the Future, from Ancient Oracles to AI (2026). That fight intensified this week with the publication of our Commission on 21st century global threats to health. Commissioners reviewed almost 400 risks to human health. They identified two existential threats and 15 major catastrophic threats. The peer review process was instructive about how these findings might be received.

items.title: [Perspectives] Shadows and interiority
items.summary: American television series The Pitt may have redefined the popularity of medical drama, but hospitals have always provided a rich seam for creatives, whether their medium is page or screen. From novels like Aleksandr Solzhenitsyn's 1966 Soviet-era Cancer Ward and Abraham Verghese's epic saga Cutting for Stone (2009) all the way through to television dramas such as Casualty, ER, and Grey's Anatomy, it seems we can’t get enough of human stories played out in a tense clinical setting. This is the absolute opposite of what author Chloe Aridjis does in The Shadow of the Object.

items.title: [Perspectives] Beyond the battlefield: war and global health security
items.summary: During the Syrian war (2011–24), the Assad Government forces and their Russian allies conducted hundreds of strikes on medical facilities in opposition-held areas. Monitoring groups documented over 600 attacks on health care, resulting in the deaths of hundreds of health-care workers throughout the conflict. Hospitals in eastern Aleppo and other contested regions were reduced to rubble. Surgeons operated in underground rooms illuminated by generators, and ambulances were targeted while transporting patients between sites.

items.title: [Perspectives] Temporal rationing: a man with gastric cancer in Colombia
items.summary: Pepe, a 45-year-old man living in the city of Cali, Colombia, worked as a self-employed hauler of goods with a wheelbarrow. In 2010, he presented to a general practitioner with several months of abdominal heaviness and non-exertional substernal burning. The physician provisionally diagnosed gastro-oesophageal reflux disease and prescribed omeprazole. However, Pepe's symptoms slowly worsened and 10 weeks later he returned to the physician, who ordered a gastroscopy, which occurred 2 months later, revealing an ulcerated mass.

items.title: [Correspondence] WHO should adjust its cervical cancer plan – Authors’ reply
items.summary: We agree with Eric J Suba that current global inequalities in cervical cancer burden are driven largely by unequal access to effective screening programmes. This point was highlighted by Brisson and colleagues1 and in an accompanying Comment2 that warned that human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination implementation must not follow the same inequitable path.

items.title: Spiny dogfish blood contains a hormone long thought absent in sharks
items.summary: Cortisol is a hormone that helps humans and many other animals regulate their energy use and respond to changing conditions. For a long time, sharks and rays were believed to rely on a different steroid hormone for these functions, without producing cortisol themselves. items.title: Supercooled clouds over the highest mountains respond differently to climate change
items.summary: Most studies of how clouds are responding to climate change focus on clouds over the oceans, rather than over mountains. Those that do focus on mountain clouds tend to explore cloud microphysics rather than long-term trends in cloud phase. But understanding cloud behavior over regions such as the Tibetan Plateau, which supplies water to hundreds of millions of people, is critical—especially as diminishing snowpack and altered precipitation patterns threaten this critical water source.

items.title: NASA's Hubble spies spiral's edge
items.summary: This NASA Hubble Space Telescope image features the edge-on, intermediate spiral galaxy NGC 1827, located roughly 37 million light-years away in the constellation Columba, the Dove. Hubble captured the image as part of a survey looking at 260 satellite galaxies around 22 Milky Way–like host galaxies within a radius of about 32 million light-years from Earth. Hubble has already observed 111 of these satellite galaxies. The remaining galaxies will take an additional 149 Hubble orbits, one orbit for each galaxy, to observe.

items.title: Forecasting 'tipping points' with AI climate simulation
items.summary: The writer Malcolm Gladwell popularized the term "tipping points" to refer to the moment when a trend or social behavior crosses a threshold and rapidly spreads everywhere. In physics, tipping points occur when systems—say, Earth's climate—reach an unstable point and topple over into a sea of change that is sometimes irreversible. Examples include global warming or the melting of polar ice caps.

items.title: 70 % de l’eau de Guadeloupe n’atteint jamais les robinets : 80 000 habitants privés d’eau
items.summary: En Guadeloupe, près de 80 000 habitants sont régulièrement privés d'eau, contraints de se ravitailler dans des stations mises en place par les mairies. En cause : un réseau vétuste et des “tuyaux-passoire”. 70% de l’eau produite sur l'île n’atteint jamais les robinets. Le réseau est en cours de réparation, mais au rythme actuel, la Cour des comptes estime qu'il faudrait 208 ans pour le renouveler entièrement. Une information judiciaire s’est ouverte à Paris le 24 septembre sur cette crise.

Comme ailleurs en Amérique du Sud, les habitants des zones à risques sont appelés à évacuer. El Niño entraîne une hausse des températures à la surface de l'océan Pacifique, perturbe les régimes de vent et de précipitations à l'échelle planétaire et cause déjà de gigantesques feux de forêts en Indonésie, et l'intensification de la sécheresse à Madagascar.

Current evaluations score the co-evolved policy on the final bank it trained with (the delivered bank). After deployment, however, skills may be rewritten, added or removed more frequently than the policy model is retrained, leaving the policy to operate on a drifted skill bank that neither the training objective nor existing evaluation protocols address. items.title: A Multi-Tiered AI Accessibility Model (MAIAM): Proportionate Access and Capability Limits for Comprehensive Frontier AI Safety
items.summary: arXiv:2610.20921v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Most debate about releasing capable AI systems treats the choice as binary: keep the model behind an API, or publish the weights. items.title: [Editorial] Rethinking threats to human survival
items.summary: Much health advocacy is driven by single-issue activism. Communities with a common interest—from AIDS to child health, climate to tobacco control—focus intensely on their own domain. And understandably so. Important progress has been made through often courageous direct action. But this sharply competitive approach is, according to a new Lancet Commission on 21st Century Global Threats to Health, dangerously flawed. Indeed, perhaps the most important contribution of this Commission is to move global health beyond the consideration of individual harms.

items.title: [Editorial] Rethinking lived experience
items.summary: The theme of this year's World Mental Health Day, held on Oct 10, is Lived experiences heard: real voices, real change. On its website, WHO states that the voices of people with lived experience should “shape the policies, services and decisions that affect their lives”. While these are laudable aims, they also serve to highlight the complex challenges involved in lived experience engagement and co-production, both within the field of mental health and beyond.

items.title: [Comment] Retatrutide in adults with obesity and type 2 diabetes: what have we learned from TRIUMPH-2?
items.summary: It is a general observation that the degree of weight loss obtained with GLP-1 receptor agonists is less in individuals with type 2 diabetes than in people without diabetes and similar BMI. Could this difference be overcome with the new triple agonists with superior weight-lowering effects? The TRIUMPH-2 study by Virginia Bellido and colleagues1 in The Lancet is a double-blind, parallel-group, randomised, placebo-controlled, phase 3 trial of the effects of retatrutide, a triple agonist (GLP-1, GIP, and glucagon), in people with obesity and type 2 diabetes.

items.title: [Articles] Status, challenges, and future directions of machine learning in the management of epilepsy: a systematic review and meta-analysis
items.summary: Although machine learning shows promise in predicting epilepsy treatment outcomes, the high heterogeneity and bias—particularly in small sample sizes, handling of missing data, and scarcity of studies with external validation—limit its clinical applicability. Future research should focus on larger, diverse datasets and standardised minimum reporting. Prospective trials are needed to evaluate machine learning models in real-world settings.

items.title: [Review] Machine learning prediction for epilepsy treatment selection and prognosis: achievements and challenges
items.summary: Accurate prediction of treatment response and selection of optimal treatments remain challenging in epilepsy management. With no reliable surrogate biomarkers for treatment response, the current process of selecting an antiseizure medication remains largely a trial-and-error approach. Other non-pharmacological treatment options, such as epilepsy surgery, are viable alternatives for patients with drug-resistant epilepsy. Statistical and machine learning techniques have been used to predict seizure outcomes associated with antiseizure medications and epilepsy surgery.
